account: Orbis International and the Rwanda International Institute of Ophthalmology ran the RAIDERS randomized trial at four diabetes clinics in and around Kigali, Rwanda. Screening ran from March to June 2021, and follow-up continued through July 2021. Retinal images went to Cybersight AI, a grading service that Orbis offers free to eye health professionals in low- and middle-income countries and that returns a result within 60 seconds. The 275 adults whom the AI judged to need referral were randomly assigned to receive the AI result and referral advice at once or to receive referral advice after human grading three to five days later. Within 30 days, 70 of 136 people (51.5%) in the immediate group attended the referral service, against 55 of 139 (39.6%) in the delayed group (P = 0.048). The trial was small and short. Several authors are employees of Orbis, which provides the AI service.

ai_role.statement: People who needed referral were randomly assigned to immediate AI feedback or to delayed human grading, so the difference in uptake is attributable to the immediate AI result.
